claims.text: The initial material is a 3D-printed W foam with 60% porosity.
The W foam has an approximately 200 µm strut diameter.
Galvanostatic Cu electrodeposition from a CuSO4 bath can fully infiltrate and coat the W foam.
Electrodeposition produces a conformal Cu layer on the W skeleton.
The electrodeposited Cu layer is epitaxial on W.
The Cu layer bridges W struts.
The conformal Cu layer eliminates interfacial voids.
Electrochemical nucleation and growth of Cu on W produces full wetting and intimate W–Cu contact.
Intimate W–Cu contact reduces thermal boundary resistance.
The proposed route achieves the interface without high-temperature sintering.
The electrodeposited composite will have thermal conductivity of at least 330 W/m·K.
The electrodeposited composite will have at least 10% higher thermal conductivity than the spark-plasma-sintered baseline.
The electrodeposited composite will have an interfacial void fraction below 1%.
The electrodeposited composite will retain mechanical strength within 10% of the baseline.
A spark-plasma-sintered W–Cu composite containing 50 vol% W has thermal conductivity of approximately 300 W/m·K.
The proposed deposition is performed at 25 °C and 50 mA/cm² for 2 hours.
The proposed processing window covers W strut diameters of 100–500 µm and current densities of 25–100 mA/cm².
The proposed service-temperature boundary is 400 °C or below.
The proposed irradiation boundary is 1 dpa or below.
The composite retains mechanical durability under the stated fusion-joint service conditions.

contradictions.description: A fully filled 60%-porous W foam would nominally contain about 40 vol% W, whereas the named baseline contains 50 vol% W. The experiment also describes SPS of W and Cu powders while calling the compared W foams identical, so the claimed compositionally and structurally controlled comparison is internally unclear.
